questions.questionText:
Four students make statements about the mass of an object.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: The mass of an object depends on the gravitational field which acts on the object.
The mass of an object divided by its weight is equal to the acceleration with which it falls freely.
The mass of an object increases when the temperature of the object increases.
The mass of an object resists change in motion of the object.

What does this mean?

It uses very little energy.
It wastes very little energy.
It works very quickly.

questions.questionText:
At room temperature, iron is difficult to compress.
At the same temperature, oxygen is much easier to compress.
Which comparison of the structures of iron and oxygen explains this?

options.text: The iron particles are closer together.
The iron particles have a greater mass.
The iron particles can be magnetised.
The iron particles have less average kinetic energy.

questions.questionText:
A night storage heater contains a large block of material that is heated electrically during the
night. During the day the block cools down, releasing thermal energy into the room.
Which thermal capacity and which night-time temperature increase will cause the most energy to
be stored by the block?
thermal capacity night-time
of block temperature increase

options.text: large large
large small
small large
small small

questions.questionText:
The handle of a metal saucepan is made of plastic. As the saucepan heats up, the handle gets
warmer.
Which statement explains this?

options.text: Molecules of the plastic radiate their energy to other molecules.
Molecules of the plastic vibrate more and pass on their energy to nearby molecules.
The free electrons in the plastic transfer the thermal energy along the handle.
The heated molecules very slowly move along the plastic handle.

questions.questionText:
The metal surface of a kettle is hot.
What happens to the cool air outside the kettle when it comes into contact with the hot kettle?

options.text: The density of the air decreases and the air falls.
The density of the air decreases and the air rises.
The density of the air increases and the air falls.
The density of the air increases and the air rises.

questions.questionText:
Vacuum flasks usually have silvered walls that help to keep the contents of the flask hot.
Why are the walls silvered?

options.text: to absorb thermal energy from the air around the flask
to increase the rate of convection inside the flask
to reduce energy loss to the surroundings by conduction
to reflect thermal radiation back into the flask

questions.questionText:
An eclipse of the Sun happens when the Moon comes between the Earth and the Sun.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: Infra-red radiation from the Sun disappears before visible light and ultra-violet radiation.
Ultra-violet radiation from the Sun disappears before visible light and infra-red radiation.
Visible light from the Sun disappears before ultra-violet radiation and infra-red radiation.
Infra-red radiation, ultra-violet radiation and visible light from the Sun all disappear at the same moment.

questions.questionText:
An observer stands at the finish line of a 100m race. He wants to time the winner’s run. He starts
his stop-watch as soon as he sees the smoke from the starting gun instead of when he hears the
bang.
What is the reason for doing this?

options.text: Light travels much faster than sound.
There is a risk he might respond to an echo from a wall.
Humans react slower to sound than to light.
Humans react more quickly to sound than to light.

questions.questionText:
A soft iron bar is a long way from any magnetic field.
How can the material of the bar be described?

options.text: It is magnetic and strongly magnetised.
It is magnetic and unmagnetised.
It is non-magnetic and strongly magnetised.
It is non-magnetic and unmagnetised.
